column2: Video checkpoint 1: running container shown on EC2, `nmap -sV -Pn -p T:25565 <public-ip>` output shows port open with Minecraft service responding and MOTD containing name or student ID, and host reboot followed by confirmed auto-recovery.
column6: All three elements clearly shown: running container, nmap output with correct MOTD, and confirmed reboot auto-recovery.
column9: Two of three elements clearly shown, or one element is ambiguous (e.g., MOTD missing name, reboot timing unclear, or auto-recovery not confirmed).
column12: Fewer than two elements shown or no credible evidence of reachability or auto-recovery.

column2: Video checkpoint 2: marker file placed in world directory and `level.dat` modification time noted, then container stopped, removed, and recreated; marker file and `level.dat` timestamp confirmed unchanged after recreate.
column6: Marker placed, full container stop-remove-recreate lifecycle shown, and both marker survival and `level.dat` timestamp unchanged clearly visible.
column9: Persistence demonstrated but one step is missing or ambiguous (e.g., `level.dat` timestamp not shown, or container was only restarted rather than removed and recreated).
column12: No credible persistence proof shown or world data appears lost.

column2: Video checkpoint 3: upgrade from one pinned ECR image version to a newer version shown with health validation, then rollback to the prior known-good version confirmed without rebuilding from scratch.
column6: Both upgrade and rollback performed with distinct version tags; health validation shown after upgrade; rollback confirmed with prior version running.
column9: One operation (upgrade or rollback) is clearly shown but the other is weak or omitted, or version tags are ambiguous.
column12: No credible upgrade and rollback sequence demonstrated.

column2: Video checkpoint 4: world data backup artifact uploaded to S3 bucket, then a restore from that backup to the live service demonstrated with service confirmed healthy after restore.
column6: Backup upload to S3 and restore from S3 both clearly shown; service confirmed healthy after restore.
column9: Backup upload shown but restore not demonstrated, or restore shown but S3 source is ambiguous or service health not confirmed.
column12: No credible S3 backup upload and restore demonstrated.

column2: Evaluated on four elements: (1) run definition is reproducible (`docker-compose.yml`, `docker run` command, or equivalent), (2) runtime config is externalized via environment variables or mounted config file, (3) restart-on-reboot mechanism is configured (restart policy or systemd unit), (4) `25565/tcp` is exposed and accessible to clients.
column6: All four elements present and correctly configured.
column9: Three of four elements present and correctly configured; one minor gap.
column12: Two of four elements present; significant missing configuration remains.
column15: Fewer than two elements present or container definition is not reproducibly runnable.

column2: Evaluated on four elements: (1) at least two distinct versioned images exist in ECR, (2) tagging scheme is immutable and consistent (e.g., `mc-1.21.1-build7`), (3) deployments pin a specific version tag (`latest`-only deployments do not qualify), (4) upstream image provenance is documented and justified as trusted.
column6: All four elements present and correct.
column9: Three of four elements present; one area is incomplete or inconsistent.
column12: Two of four elements present; version discipline or provenance is substantially incomplete.
column15: Fewer than two elements present or no meaningful version discipline demonstrated.

column2: Evaluated on three elements: (1) backup artifact uploaded to a private S3 bucket (no public ACL or bucket policy), (2) at least one S3 lifecycle rule configured with a documented justification for the chosen retention period, (3) restore procedure is documented step-by-step and reproducible.
column6: All three elements present and correctly configured.
column9: Two of three elements present; one is missing or underdeveloped.
column12: Only one element clearly present; backup or restore workflow is substantially incomplete.
column15: No credible private S3 backup, restore, or retention setup demonstrated.

column2: Evaluated on three elements: (1) pre-change checklist explicitly includes S3 backup of world data as a mandatory step before any upgrade, (2) post-change validation steps are listed with expected healthy outcomes, (3) rollback procedure is operationally distinct from a fresh install (pulls and runs an existing ECR image without rebuilding or reinstalling).
column6: All three elements present and clearly executable by another operator.
column9: Two of three elements present; one is vague, incomplete, or missing.
column12: Only one element clearly present; runbook is not operationally usable as written.
column15: Upgrade and rollback runbook is absent or meets none of the three elements.

column2: All five required sections present (build+publish workflow, ECR usage and image tag policy, runtime architecture diagram, S3 backup/restore runbook, upgrade and rollback runbook with pre/post validation), and procedures are conceptual and actionable rather than a raw command dump that another operator could not follow without guesswork.
column6: All five sections present, correctly ordered, and operator-ready; another TA could execute the procedures without asking clarifying questions.
column9: Four of five sections complete, or one section has a minor gap; overall usable by a new operator.
column12: Three of five sections complete or multiple sections require significant inference; not reliably usable by another operator.
column15: Fewer than three sections present or documentation is not executable by another operator.
